todo_crud.idea: A habit tracker with streaks, badges, dark mode, and weekly reports

api_endpoints.description: Register a new user
Login an existing user
Get all habits for the current user
Create a new habit
Get a specific habit
Update a habit
Delete a habit
Mark a habit as completed
Get a weekly report of habit completions
Populate the database with demo data
Get summary statistics

features: Register, login, and JWT‑based authentication for all endpoints
Create, read, update, and delete habits owned by the authenticated user
Mark a habit as completed for the current day and automatically compute streaks

user_stories.want: to sign up and log in
acceptance_criteria: POST /auth/register with email and password returns 201 and a JWT token
POST /auth/login with valid credentials returns 200 and a JWT token
Accessing any /habits endpoint without a JWT returns 401 Unauthorized

user_stories.want: to create a new habit
acceptance_criteria: POST /habits with a name (and optional description) returns 201 and the created habit object
The returned habit includes a user_id that matches the authenticated user
Missing required fields (e.g., name) returns 400 Bad Request

user_stories.want: to mark a habit as completed for today
acceptance_criteria: POST /habits/{habit_id}/complete returns 200 and the habit's updated streak_count
If the habit was already marked complete for the current day, the endpoint returns 409 Conflict
If the previous day was missed, the streak_count resets to 1

user_stories.want: to view my habit list with current streaks and badge status
acceptance_criteria: GET /habits returns 200 and an array of the user's habits
Each habit object includes name, streak_count, last_completed_at, and badge fields
Only habits belonging to the authenticated user are returned

user_stories.want: to receive a weekly report summarizing my habit completions
acceptance_criteria: GET /habits/weekly-report returns 200 and a JSON object listing each habit with a count of completions in the last 7 days
The report also includes the current streak_count and any badge earned for each habit
The endpoint requires a valid JWT and returns 401 if missing

user_stories.want: to switch the UI to dark mode
acceptance_criteria: A toggle in the UI changes the theme to dark and persists the choice in local storage
When the app is reopened, the stored preference is applied automatically
No additional API calls are required for theme changes

user_stories.want: to earn badges when I reach streak milestones
acceptance_criteria: When streak_count reaches 7, the badge field updates to "7‑Day Streak"
When streak_count reaches 30, the badge field updates to "30‑Day Streak"
Badge updates are reflected in the habit list returned by GET /habits

user_stories.want: to delete a habit I no longer need
acceptance_criteria: DELETE /habits/{habit_id} returns 204 No Content
The habit is no longer present in subsequent GET /habits responses
Attempting to delete a habit that does not belong to the user returns 404 Not Found

non_functional_requirements.authentication: required — all habit endpoints must be accessed with a valid JWT
non_functional_requirements.authorization: users can only access, modify, or delete habits that belong to them
non_functional_requirements.pagination: optional on GET /habits if the user has many habits

api_endpoints.description: Populates database with realistic demo data.
Returns aggregate counts and key metrics for the dashboard.
Authenticates a user and returns a JWT token.
Retrieves the profile of the currently authenticated user.
Retrieves a paginated list of all published blog posts, with optional tag filtering.
Retrieves a single published blog post by its ID.

Updates an existing blog post by its ID.

features: Secure login for authors and role-based access control to ensure authors can only manage their own posts and readers can only view published content.
Authors can create new posts with title, markdown content, tags, and a cover image URL, and edit existing posts.
Authors can save posts as drafts for later editing and explicitly publish them when ready, making them visible to readers.
Authors can delete their own posts, removing them from the system.
Readers can view a list of all published posts, displaying title, author, date, and tags.

user_stories.want: to create a new blog post
acceptance_criteria: I can input a title, markdown content, tags, and a cover image URL.
The post is saved as a 'draft' by default upon creation.
I receive confirmation that my post has been successfully created.

user_stories.want: to save a post as a draft
acceptance_criteria: When I save a post, its status is set to 'draft'.
Draft posts are not visible to readers.
I can access and edit my draft posts from my author dashboard.

user_stories.want: to publish a draft post
acceptance_criteria: I can change the status of a draft post to 'published'.
The published post immediately appears in the list of posts visible to readers.
The published post displays its title, my name, the publication date, and its tags.

user_stories.want: to edit an existing post (draft or published)
acceptance_criteria: I can modify the title, content, tags, and cover image URL of any of my posts.
If the post is published, the changes are reflected immediately for readers.
I receive confirmation that my post has been successfully updated.

user_stories.want: to view a list of all published blog posts
acceptance_criteria: I see a list of posts, each displaying its title, author, publication date, and tags.
Only 'published' posts are visible in this list.
The list is ordered by publication date, newest first.

user_stories.want: to filter posts by a specific tag
acceptance_criteria: I can select a tag to filter the post list.
Only posts containing the selected tag are displayed.
The filter can be cleared to show all published posts again.

user_stories.want: to read a full blog post
acceptance_criteria: When I click on a post title, I am taken to a dedicated page for that post.
The full content (markdown rendered), title, author, publication date, and cover image are displayed.
The post's tags are also visible on the individual post page.

non_functional_requirements.authentication: required — Authors need to log in to manage posts; Readers do not need to log in to view posts.
non_functional_requirements.authorization: Authors can only create, edit, delete, and publish their own posts. Readers can only view published posts.
non_functional_requirements.pagination: required on: /posts (for readers), /authors/{author_id}/posts (for authors)

acceptance_criteria: GET /vehicles?maintenance_alert=true returns only vehicles where fuel_consumption_rate increased >20% over last 7 days
Each returned vehicle includes maintenance_due date
Alert list is paginated

user_stories.want: generate a compliance report showing vehicles with overdue maintenance
acceptance_criteria: GET /vehicles/compliance_report returns list of vehicles where maintenance_due < today
Each entry includes license_plate and days_overdue
Report can be exported as CSV via query param format=csv

user_stories.want: update the fuel level after refueling
acceptance_criteria: PATCH /vehicles/{id} with fuel_level field updates the record
Response returns updated fuel_level and last_fuel_update timestamp
If driver not assigned to vehicle, API returns 403
